metaDescription: Six 20V cordless string trimmers compared on cutting swath, line feed, weight and battery size, with picks for small lawns and edging-heavy yards.
expertTake: The CRAFTSMAN V20 13 inch trimmer is the best overall because its wider swath and larger battery finish a yard faster than the 10 and 12 inch class. The BLACK+DECKER 2-in-1 is the value pick for small lawns. If your yard has heavy brush, tall weeds or more than a quarter acre of edges, skip 20V string trimmers entirely and step up to a 40V or 56V model.
introParagraphs: A cordless string trimmer spins a length of nylon line fast enough to slice grass and weeds, and the line does the cutting while the motor and battery supply the speed. Box specs like RPM and cutting width suggest more than they deliver, because torque and line feed decide what happens in thick growth.

This guide explains the specs that matter on a 20V class trimmer: swath, line feed, shaft design and battery size. Check the picks above for a shortlist, then read the reviews below for where each one fits and where it falls short.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 13 Inch String Trimmer and Edger Kit
products.description:
Craftsman's 13 inch kit leads on the two specs that matter most in a 20V trimmer: swath and battery. A 13 inch swath cuts a wider path per pass than the 12 inch units here, and the included 4.0Ah battery is about double the capacity of the smaller packs in the class.

The claimed runtime of up to 63 minutes is a light-load figure, but a 4.0Ah pack genuinely goes further than a 2.0Ah pack on the same motor. The motor is rated for more power than the earlier Craftsman design, which helps in thick grass. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER 12 inch wheeled unit, which ships with a 2.5Ah battery, the Craftsman packs much more runtime.

The adjustable handle suits a range of heights. V20 batteries fit a wide family of Craftsman tools, so one pack covers more than the trimmer. Maintenance is straightforward: replace the line, clear the guard and store the battery indoors.
products.bestFor: Medium yards where a wider swath and long runtime reduce the number of passes and charges.
pros: 13 in swath is the widest in this group
4.0Ah battery gives the best runtime in the box
Adjustable handle fits different user heights
Batteries work with the broader V20 range
cons: Larger swath adds a little weight and bulk
Light-load runtime claims will not hold in thick growth

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX 12 Inch Trimmer and Wheeled Edger
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER kit uses a PowerDrive transmission, which boosts torque at the string rather than raising raw RPM. That matters because string cutting depends on torque more than speed, and a transmission that preserves speed under load keeps the line from bogging in thick grass.

A dual speed control lets you choose higher power for tough areas or a lower setting for longer runtime. The 2.5Ah battery is a step up from the 1.5Ah class but below the Craftsman's 4.0Ah. Automatic line feed removes the need to bump the head, and the wheeled edger mode helps keep straight lines along walks.

Because 20V MAX is a widely stocked platform, replacement packs are easy to find. Check the line spool regularly and clean the guard of clippings.
products.bestFor: Small to medium yards that need a trimmer and a wheeled edger in one tool.
pros: PowerDrive transmission boosts torque at the string
Dual speed control balances power and runtime
Automatic line feed removes the need to bump the head
Wheeled edger mode keeps straight lines on walks
cons: 2.5Ah battery gives less runtime than the Craftsman
12 in swath is narrower than the Craftsman's 13 in

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX 2-in-1 String Trimmer and Edger
products.description:
This is the simple, small-yard trimmer in the lineup. The automatic feed spool advances line as it wears, and the unit converts from trimmer to edger in seconds. For tidying around beds, fences and a small lawn, that is all most homeowners need.

Like the 12 inch BLACK+DECKER with the wheeled edger, it uses a PowerDrive transmission, which delivers more torque to the line. It lacks the larger battery of that model and the Craftsman, so expect shorter runs. It is the straightforward, established-brand option.

Support is a plus, since the 20V MAX platform has replacement batteries widely available. Keep the guard clear and refill line when it runs low.
products.bestFor: Small yards and light weekly tidying with minimal fuss.
pros: Automatic feed spool means no bumping the head
Converts between trimming and edging in seconds
PowerDrive transmission helps torque at the line
Established platform with easy battery replacement
cons: Smaller battery limits runtime on bigger yards
Not meant for heavy weeds or brush

products.name: WORX WG154 20V 10 Inch 2-in-1 String Trimmer and Edger
products.description:
At 4.2 pounds, the WG154 is the lightest trimmer in the lineup, which makes a real difference to how long you can work comfortably. It has a 10 inch swath, the narrowest here, so you trade coverage for ease.

The head rotates 180 degrees to switch between trimming and edging, and you can choose a narrower cut for longer runtime or a wider cut for faster work. Automatic line feed spares you from tapping the spool. It sits in the WORX PowerShare family, so batteries from other WORX tools work in it.

It suits small yards and people who tire easily. For anything more than a quarter acre, a wider swath and bigger battery help. Check the line spool and clear the guard.
products.bestFor: Small yards and users who put a premium on light weight and easy handling.
pros: 4.2 lb is the lightest trimmer in this roundup
Rotating head switches to edging in one move
Selectable cut width trades speed for runtime
Batteries are shared across the PowerShare range
cons: 10 in swath needs more passes on bigger lawns
Smaller battery limits runtime on large yards

products.name: HEYWORK 20V 12 Inch Cordless String Trimmer and Edger Kit
products.description:
HEYWORK bundles two 4.0Ah batteries and a charger with a 12 inch trimmer, which is the largest total energy in the roundup. For a bigger yard, that means you can swap packs mid-job rather than waiting for a charge.

A stated 8,000 RPM motor gives high line speed, though again RPM alone does not guarantee torque. At 6.3 pounds with an adjustable grip, it is heavier than the 4.2 pound WORX, and about the same as typical 12 inch trimmers. It switches between trimming and edging.

The tradeoff is brand support, since it is a lesser-known name. Check battery availability, keep the guard clear and replace the line as needed.
products.bestFor: Larger yards where two big batteries matter more than brand heritage.
pros: Two 4.0Ah batteries give the most total energy here
Automatic line feed removes the need to bump
8,000 RPM motor keeps line speed high
Converts between trimmer and edger modes
cons: 6.3 lb is heavier than the lightest options
Lesser-known brand with unproven battery supply
RPM claim does not guarantee torque in thick growth

products.name: LPSUK 20V 12 Inch 3-in-1 Trimmer, Edger and Mower
products.description:
This unit adds a third mode, a light mowing configuration, to the usual trimmer and edger. A telescopic shaft runs from 38 to 49 inches, so it fits a range of heights, which reduces back strain.

Two 2.0Ah batteries with a fast charger that fills in about 1 hour 20 minutes are modest in capacity, less than half of the HEYWORK pair. The mower mode is a convenience for small patches, not a substitute for a mower.

It is the choice for someone who wants three tools in one for a tiny yard. Brand support is limited, so check parts and battery availability. Keep the guard and line clean.
products.bestFor: Tiny yards that benefit from a light mowing mode and a height-adjustable shaft.
pros: Telescopic shaft from 38 to 49 in suits many heights
Three modes cover trim, edge and light mowing
Fast charger fills a pack in about 80 minutes
Auto line feed means no bumping
cons: Mower mode is only for small patches

buyingCriteria.explanation: Swath is the diameter of the circle the line cuts, and a wider swath covers more ground per pass. On open lawn, 13 inches saves meaningful time compared with 10 inches, but a wide swath is harder to place close to fences and beds. Buyers often pick on swath alone and forget handling. The CRAFTSMAN is 13 inches, the BLACK+DECKER 12 inch, HEYWORK and LPSUK are 12 inches, and the WORX WG154 is 10 inches.

Line speed matters, but torque keeps it from bogging when the line meets thick grass or weeds. A transmission can multiply torque at the head, and that matters more than an impressive RPM figure. Treat RPM claims cautiously, because brushed motors in this class rarely maintain them under load. The BLACK+DECKER models use a PowerDrive transmission to add torque, while HEYWORK and LPSUK advertise 8,000 RPM.

A 2.0Ah pack in a string trimmer typically gives a short run, enough for a small lawn but not a full yard. Doubling the capacity roughly doubles the run, and a second pack lets you keep working. Check the amp-hours in the box, not just the voltage. The HEYWORK ships with two 4.0Ah packs and the CRAFTSMAN with one 4.0Ah pack, while the LPSUK ships with two 2.0Ah packs.

A trimmer swings from side to side, and weight at the head and battery location affect fatigue. Under five pounds is easy for most users, while over six pounds begins to tire shoulders on long sessions. The WORX WG154 is lightest at 4.2 pounds, and the HEYWORK at 6.3 pounds is among the heaviest.

Automatic feed advances line as it wears, saving the bump-and-tap routine. Systems vary in reliability, and a good one avoids jamming and wasting line. A push-button feed is a fine alternative to fully automatic feeding. Most trimmers here use automatic feed, including the BLACK+DECKER units, WORX and HEYWORK.

Many 20V trimmers convert to edgers by rotating the head or folding a wheel. A true wheeled edger keeps a straight line along walks better than a rotating head used freehand. Edging mode uses the same line, so it is a trim-line cut, not a blade edge. The BLACK+DECKER 12 inch includes a wheel, while the WORX rotates its head 180 degrees.

specDecoder.meaning: The diameter of the cutting circle traced by the line. A wider swath trims more ground in each pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: A wide swath on a weak motor bogs down. The 13 inch CRAFTSMAN pairs a wide swath with a stronger motor.

specDecoder.meaning: How fast the head spins. Higher RPM raises line speed, which helps slice grass cleanly.
specDecoder.watchFor: 8,000 RPM claims on the HEYWORK and LPSUK are no-load figures and fall under load.

specDecoder.meaning: A gear stage between motor and head that raises torque delivered to the line, helping it keep speed in thick growth.
specDecoder.watchFor: It is a BLACK+DECKER feature, and not all trimmers with high RPM have a comparable torque advantage.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. More Ah means more stored energy and longer runtime at the same load.
specDecoder.watchFor: Runtime claims such as the CRAFTSMAN's 63 minutes are light-load figures.

specDecoder.meaning: A mechanism that releases fresh line as it wears, so you do not need to bump the head.
specDecoder.watchFor: Quality varies, and a poor system can waste line or jam. Look for consistent owner feedback.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swath, motor type and any torque-boosting transmission. The CRAFTSMAN's 13 inch swath and stronger motor led, while the WORX's 10 inch swath trailed on coverage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared included battery capacity and number of packs. The HEYWORK's two 4.0Ah packs and the CRAFTSMAN's 4.0Ah battery led, and the LPSUK's two 2.0Ah packs trailed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights and shaft adjustability. The WORX WG154 at 4.2 pounds led, and the LPSUK's telescopic shaft scored for fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered platform size and battery availability. The CRAFTSMAN, BLACK+DECKER and WORX platforms scored higher than the smaller brands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read patterns in owner feedback for line feed jams, battery fade and head wobble. Where spec sheets and feedback disagreed, we weighted the pattern from owners.

howToChoose.intro: Yard size sets swath and battery needs.

rows: Small patio and flower bed edges
Tiny yard with patches to mow

cards.label: Wheeled edger
cards.text: A wheel rides on the walk and keeps the line straight, giving a cleaner edge with less skill. The BLACK+DECKER 12 inch uses this approach.

cards.label: Rotating head edger
cards.text: You turn the head 90 or 180 degrees and guide it freehand, which is lighter but takes practice. The WORX WG154 and the HEYWORK do this.

howToChoose.note: If you edge long walks regularly, take the wheeled unit; for occasional edging, a rotating head is fine.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A light tool, automatic line feed and enough battery for one session. Small lawns do not need a wide swath, and ease of handling matters more.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WORX WG154 and BLACK+DECKER 2-in-1 are the lightest, simplest choices. If you also want longer runtime, the CRAFTSMAN 13 inch is the stronger choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your yard is larger than a quarter acre or you cut thick grass. The CRAFTSMAN 13 inch kit gives the widest swath and best battery, and a bigger platform keeps packs available.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a small yard weekly. The BLACK+DECKER 2-in-1 or WORX WG154 do that job at lower cost.

maintenance.interval: As it wears, usually every few sessions
maintenance.why: Worn line cuts poorly and strains the motor. Use the line diameter the maker specifies.
Packed grass causes heat and uneven line. A quick wipe prevents it.
A cracked spool jams or releases line unevenly. Replace damaged spools.
Lithium packs age fastest empty or hot. Keep them indoors.
Loose joints cause wobble and vibration. Tighten fasteners as needed.

faq.q: Is a 13 inch swath better than 10 inches?
faq.a: For open lawns, yes, since each pass covers more. For tight beds, 10 to 12 inches is easier to place.
Basic kits cost the least, and larger batteries and wider swaths cost more. Count batteries in the total, and spend more for bigger yards.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Small 2.0Ah packs give a short run, while 4.0Ah packs go much further. Light-load runtime claims will not hold in thick growth.

faq.q: Is RPM a good measure of power?
faq.a: Not alone. Torque keeps the line from bogging, and a transmission can matter more than a high RPM figure.

faq.q: Can a 20V trimmer handle thick weeds?
faq.a: Only light to moderate growth. For thick brush, step up to a 40V or higher model, or a brush cutter.
Yes. Trimmer line throws debris at speed, so wear safety glasses and sturdy shoes.
